text: And this was indeed observed also experimentally, years ago. Some researchers made experiments with different Wi-Fi cards, which were commercial products. They claimed all these cards claim to follow the standard, for products must follow the standard. They claim to do that, but actually one of these cards was applying everything, okay, as specified by the standard, but the post pickoff. And what these researchers observed was that this Wi-Fi card was obtaining a very very high throughput, that means the ability to transmit a lot of data, while the other Wi-Fi cards were starving, so they could not get access to the channel. A very unfair service, and this is because this was because that commercial Wi-Fi card at that time did not implement the post pickoff procedure. So this seems to be you know a detail or one more thing that and no that has to do, but it's actually extremely important to ensure fairness. In Wi-Fi, we want to be fair, we want to give the same probability to everyone in channel access. So it is a very important feature, and notice that the same would happen if we didn't have the post pickoff procedure.
